title: needs-decision: wake-up discipline recurrence persists after #2179/#2210
body:
## Background

Delegated subagent workers repeatedly end their turn believing a
background wait/CI-monitoring task will resume them automatically,
when no such automatic resumption exists — the orchestrator has to
actively poll live state and re-message the worker instead. This
pattern (tracked previously under #1733, #1384, #1387, #1807, and most
recently #2210) has been addressed several times through progressively
stronger wording in the delegation-brief instructions.

A newer, independently reported run — on an `idd-skill` v0.7.0 pin
that already includes the #2179/#2210 delegation-brief strengthening —
observed the same failure recurring in nearly every delegated worker
across roughly ten delegated tasks in one session, even with an
explicit warning in the brief that cited a concrete prior sibling
failure. Recovery required active orchestrator intervention (checking
live GitHub state and sending a targeted follow-up message) every
time, with no case of the wording alone preventing the recurrence.
This is a new, more direct data point than the earlier reports: it
shows the failure surviving the most recent wording strengthening
itself, on the exact wording that fix shipped, rather than on an
older or unpatched brief.

At least four other independently operated repositories reported the
same underlying pattern in the same broad window (worker turns ending
on a mistaken assumption that a background task will resume them).

## Open question

Wording-only reinforcement of the delegation brief has now been tried
several times, including the most recent round, and the pattern still
recurs at a similar rate. This suggests the remaining fix, if any,
sits above the wording layer — for example, in how the delegation
brief's own dispatched workflow is shaped (a documented,
copy-pasteable non-blocking-snapshot-then-stop pattern was reported to
work reliably as a workaround in at least one of the independent
reports), or in how the orchestration tooling itself constrains what a
delegated worker can end its turn believing.

This issue exists to record the accumulated evidence and open the
question of which direction (further brief-template changes, a
different delegation shape, or a tooling-level constraint) is worth
pursuing next, rather than to propose or pre-select a specific fix.

## What would close this issue

A chosen direction is recorded (as a comment or an update to this
issue), and any resulting concrete follow-up work is filed as its own
separate issue referencing this one.
